answer.rationale: The low-cost vendor is the only quote that clears the 18% mandate without negotiation, and memory_c2 (the only memory I'm verifying this cycle) records that moving primary supply to that vendor last year cut unit cost sharply with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing — so the cost case is not speculative. I am not pursuing the incumbent despite memories c4, c5, c6 pointing at leverage and continuity, because the contract does not auto-renew, the mandate is hard, and renewal would not by itself close an 18% gap. I am not adding a second source (c3) or deferring (c5) because the contract expires in 14 days and the line is at 94% of committed volume with no buffer — any extra moving part during cutover raises delivery risk, which is the thing the primary objective forbids. To keep delivery risk from rising during a single-source flip on a tight buffer, I will run the switch as a small, time-boxed pilot on one work order before scaling: if pilot yield and on-time delivery hold for the first run, promote to primary; if not, fall back to incumbent month-to-month while renegotiating. This preserves an out, keeps the mandate on the table, and does not assume more than c2 actually supports.
